words.notes: mich = me (direct object), mir = to me.
Capitalized Sie means formal 'you'.
Also the neuter form of der (the).
dich = you (direct object), dir = to you.
der (masculine), die (feminine and plural), das (neuter).
es gibt = there is, there are.
uns = us.
zu Hause = at home. Before an adjective, zu means 'too': zu groß (too big).
ihn = him (direct object), ihm = to him.
Also forms the past: Ich habe gegessen (I ate).
Also adds emphasis: Das ist ja toll! (That's really great!)
in + dem = im, in + das = ins.
Used with many verbs: sich freuen (to be happy), sich setzen (to sit down).
warten auf = to wait for. Auf Wiedersehen! = Goodbye!
Sends the verb to the end: Ich weiß, dass du müde bist.
noch nicht = not yet.
Komm mal her! = Come here a second! Warst du schon mal hier? = Have you ever been here?
von + dem = vom.
werden + verb = future: Ich werde kommen (I will come).
an + dem = am, an + das = ans. am Montag = on Monday.
Ich bin da = I'm here. At the start of a clause it can also mean 'since, because'.
als + past = when (a single event or period in the past; for repeated events use wenn): Als ich klein war...
Takes the dative: aus dem Haus.
um ... zu = in order to: Ich komme, um zu helfen.

words.gloss: yes (after a negative question); but; really
words.notes: Answers a negative question with yes: Kommst du nicht? – Doch! Also softens or stresses: Komm doch!
alles = everything, alle = everyone, all.
Used instead of nicht ein: Ich habe kein Auto.
At the end of a sentence: ..., oder? = ..., right?
nach Hause = (going) home. Used for cities and countries: nach Berlin.
Used with the er/sie form of the verb: man sagt (people say).
nicht müssen = not have to (not 'must not').
ich will, er will (no -t).
Past: ging, ist gegangen. Wie geht's? = How are you? Das geht nicht = That's not possible.
Often shortened to was in speech: Ich habe was gehört.
nicht mehr = not anymore; kein ... mehr = no more ...
bei + dem = beim. bei mir = at my place.
Not English 'also' (that is auch).
Bitte? = Pardon? Bitte schön = here you are; you're welcome.
immer noch = still; für immer = forever.
vor zwei Jahren = two years ago.

words.gloss: off; going; wrong (in Was ist los?)
words.notes: Was ist los? = What's wrong? / What's going on? Los! = Go!
Not wider (against).
Danke schön / vielen Dank = thank you very much.
In questions it shows interest: Was ist denn los? As a conjunction it means 'because'.
Plural: Männer. mein Mann = my husband.
Es tut mir leid = I'm sorry. Es tut weh = It hurts.
Irregular: du siehst, er sieht. Past: sah, hat gesehen.
wen = who(m) (direct object), wem = to whom.
Capitalized Ihr means formal 'your'.
Use ihr when talking to two or more friends. euch = you (as object).
Past: kam, ist gekommen.
über + das = übers.
es gibt = there is, there are. Irregular: du gibst, er gibt.
sollte = should, ought to.
noch nie = never (before).
viel = much, viele = many. Vielen Dank = thanks a lot. More: mehr.
Not der Weg (the way, path).
leben (lowercase) = to live.
Plural: Zeiten. Hast du Zeit? = Are you free?
Sends the verb to the end: weil ich müde bin.
heute Abend = this evening, tonight.
Sends the verb to the end. Also an adverb 'with it': Hör auf damit! = Stop it!
Plural: Frauen. Frau Müller = Mrs Müller. meine Frau = my wife.
Bis bald! = See you soon! bis zu = up to.
Irregular: du lässt, er lässt. Lass mich in Ruhe! = Leave me alone! Lass uns gehen = Let's go.
Plural: Götter. Mein Gott! = My God! Gott sei Dank = Thank God.
Not the verb sein (to be).
On the phone, zwo is often said for zwei.
Alles klar? = Everything OK? Klar! = Sure!
der Morgen (capitalised) = the morning: Guten Morgen!
Plural only: die Leute.
Plural: Väter. Papa = dad.
glauben an = to believe in.
ab Montag = from Monday on. ab und zu = now and then.
Plural: Tage. Guten Tag! = Hello!
reden über = to talk about.
Er ist wohl krank = He's probably sick. Ich fühle mich wohl = I feel good.
die Liebe = love (noun).
Takes the accusative: durch den Park.
Sends the verb to the end: Ich weiß nicht, ob er kommt.
Plural: Mütter. Mama = mom.
Spoken short form of heraus / hinaus.
ein paar (lowercase) = a few. das Paar (capitalised) = the pair, the couple.
Past with sein: Was ist passiert?
denken an = to think of. Past: dachte, hat gedacht.
Also selber in speech. selbst wenn = even if.
Takes the dative: Das gehört mir. gehören zu = to be part of.
möchte = would like: Ich möchte einen Kaffee.
Takes the accusative: ohne dich.
Hör mal! = Listen! zuhören = to listen (to someone).
Komm her! = Come here! Das ist lange her = That was a long time ago. Opposite: hin.
anders (adverb) = differently.
Takes the dative: Ich helfe dir. Irregular: du hilfst, er hilft.
Plural: Nächte. Gute Nacht! = Good night!
Ich finde das gut = I think that's good.
lang (adjective) = long: ein langer Tag.
Makes a negative stronger: gar nicht = not at all.
Und weiter? = And then what? weitermachen = to keep going.
Used with the present tense: Ich wohne seit zwei Jahren hier = I've lived here for two years.
As an adjective it means 'same': die gleiche Farbe.
Du hast recht = You're right. Ist dir das recht? = Is that OK with you?
In Ordnung! = OK! All right!

words.gloss: of it; about it; from it
words.notes: da + von. Ich weiß nichts davon = I don't know anything about it.
da + für. Ich bin dafür = I'm for it.
Takes the genitive (in speech often the dative): wegen des Wetters.
Plural: Häuser. zu Hause = at home, nach Hause = (going) home.
Neuter: das Mädchen. Plural: die Mädchen.
Wo gehst du hin? = Where are you going? hin und her = back and forth. Opposite: her.
Plural: Abende. Guten Abend! = Good evening! heute Abend = tonight.
Plural: Freunde. mein Freund often means 'my boyfriend'. Freundin = female friend, girlfriend.
warten auf = to wait for.
Plural: Menschen = people. Accusative and dative: den/dem Menschen. Mensch! = Wow! / Man!
Irregular: du isst, er isst. Past: aß, hat gegessen. das Essen = food, meal.
Angst haben (vor) = to be afraid (of). Plural: Ängste.
Past: blieb, ist geblieben.
Zusammen oder getrennt? = One bill or separate? (in a restaurant)
der Tod = death. sterben = to die.
nicht dürfen = must not.
erst morgen = not until tomorrow. erst fünf = only five.

words.gloss: to be right; to be true
words.notes: Das stimmt = That's right. Stimmt so! = Keep the change!
Irregular: du nimmst, er nimmt. Past: nahm, hat genommen.
Plural: Kinder.
Past: brachte, hat gebracht.
Takes the accusative. gegen acht = around eight.
Moment mal! = Wait a minute! im Moment = at the moment.
Other cases and plural: Jungen (in speech the plural is often Jungs).
Das steht dir = That suits you. Past: stand, hat gestanden.
zur Arbeit gehen = to go to work. arbeiten = to work.
die Frage = the question. fragen nach = to ask about.
Herr Weber = Mr Weber. Other cases: Herrn. Plural: Herren.

words.gloss: with it; there; at the same time
words.notes: da + bei. Ich bin dabei = I'm in.
Wie heißt du? = What's your name? Das heißt = that means.
Plural: Familien.
Sends the verb to the end. Before a noun, use vor: vor dem Essen.
Plural: Jahre. vor zwei Jahren = two years ago.
Often shortened to mal. noch einmal = once more. auf einmal = suddenly.
Plural: Probleme.
Plural: Söhne.
Use wann in direct and indirect questions (Ich weiß nicht, wann ...). When "when" links two clauses (whenever / at the time that), use wenn or als.
fertig sein = to be done. In speech also 'exhausted'.
Also alleine in speech.
Irregular: du sprichst, er spricht. Past: sprach, hat gesprochen.

words.gloss: sorry (es tut mir leid = I'm sorry)
words.notes: Es tut mir leid = I'm sorry. etwas leid sein = to be tired of something.
Spoken short form: komm rein = come in.
Mostly spoken: Das ist halt so. Halt! on its own means Stop!
Like an adjective after a determiner: die beiden = the two of them.
Plural: Sachen, often meaning things or stuff.
Hilfe! = Help!
Endings like der: jeder Mann, jede Frau, jedes Kind. On its own, jeder = everyone.

words.gloss: gladly; (with a verb) to like doing
words.notes: Ich esse gern Fisch = I like eating fish. Gern geschehen = You're welcome.
Replaces über + it/that: Ich denke darüber nach = I'm thinking about it.

words.gloss: to hold; to stop; (halten von) to think of
words.notes: du hältst, er hält; past hielt, gehalten. Was hältst du davon? = What do you think of it?
Past participle: verstanden. Verstanden? = Got it?
nicht wahr? = isn't it? (a tag question)

words.gloss: to it; for it; with it
words.notes: Replaces zu + it/that: Ich habe keine Lust dazu = I don't feel like it.
Plural: Brüder.

words.gloss: about it; on it (with verbs like denken an)
words.notes: Replaces an + it/that. Spoken short form: dran. Du bist dran = It's your turn.
Vielen Dank = Thank you very much. Gott sei Dank = Thank God.
Comparative of gern: Ich trinke lieber Tee = I prefer tea.
auf jeden Fall = definitely; auf keinen Fall = no way.

words.gloss: all the same; (es ist mir egal) I don't care
words.notes: Never takes an ending. Egal! = Whatever!

words.gloss: to know (a person or place), be familiar with
words.notes: kennen = to know someone; wissen = to know a fact.
du vergisst, er vergisst; past vergaß, vergessen.
Echt? = Really?
Softens a question: Wer bist du eigentlich? = Who are you, anyway?
Wie viel Uhr ist es? = What time is it? um acht Uhr = at eight o'clock.
Plural: Städte. in die Stadt gehen = to go into town.
Plural: Babys.
du fährst, er fährt; past fuhr; perfect with sein: ich bin gefahren.
Like Junge: der Name, den Namen. Mein Name ist … = My name is …
Not "become" (that is werden). Past bekam, perfect bekommen.
Plural: Köpfe. Kopf hoch! = Chin up!
Comparative: kleiner.
Bis später! = See you later!
Viel Glück! = Good luck! Glück haben = to be lucky.
letzte Woche = last week; zum letzten Mal = for the last time.

words.gloss: on it; for it (with verbs like warten auf)
words.notes: Replaces auf + it/that: Ich warte darauf = I'm waiting for it. Spoken: drauf.
am Ende = in the end; zu Ende = over.
Bis bald! = See you soon!
Spoken German often uses umbringen.
Plural: Dinge.

words.gloss: to mean; to think (have an opinion)
words.notes: Was meinst du? = What do you mean? / What do you think? Not to be confused with mein (my).
Toll! = Great!
Counting: eins, zwei, drei. Before a noun: ein, eine.
Plural: Minuten.
Bist du bereit? = Are you ready? Usually after sein.
Wie weit ist es? = How far is it?
Keine Ahnung! = No idea!
Usually ein bisschen: ein bisschen Zeit = a little time.
Plural: Türen.
Plural: Autos.
The possessive of ihr (you all): euer Haus, eure Mutter.
Plural: Augen.
Singular in German: Die Polizei ist da = The police are here.
du stirbst, er stirbt; past starb; perfect with sein: ist gestorben.
Location: Er ist draußen. Movement out: raus.
Not "fast" (quick); that is schnell.
Komm runter! = Come down!
Es ist vorbei = It's over. vorbeikommen = to drop by.
du triffst, er trifft; past traf, getroffen. sich treffen = to meet up.
Noun: die Arbeit.
Bist du verrückt? = Are you crazy?
Was gibt's Neues? = What's new?
With dative for place, accusative for movement.
Mach dir keine Sorgen = Don't worry.
der einzige Weg = the only way.
Darum! = Because! (no explanation). es geht darum = it's about.
Plural: Töchter.
Plural: Ideen. Gute Idee! = Good idea!
Plural: Schwestern.
Was ist da drin? = What's in there?
Sei ruhig! = Be quiet! Bleib ruhig! = Stay calm!
Wie spät ist es? = What time is it? Comparative: später.
ziemlich gut = pretty good.
Er hat sogar gelacht = He even laughed.
Warte kurz! = Wait a moment!
Informal. Plural: Kerle.

words.gloss: to lie (be lying); to be located
words.notes: Past lag, gelegen. Das liegt an dir = That's down to you.
Ich suche meinen Schlüssel = I'm looking for my key.
Hast du je …? = Have you ever …? je mehr, desto besser = the more, the better.
Woher kommst du? = Where are you from? Woher weißt du das? = How do you know?
Adverb: lange (for a long time). Comparative: länger.
Informal; more formal: die Stelle or die Arbeit.
Also for instruments and roles: Gitarre spielen.
überhaupt nicht = not at all. Wer bist du überhaupt? = Who are you anyway?
Plural also Teufel. Was zum Teufel …? = What the hell …?
Past verlor, verloren.
Comparative größer, superlative am größten.
Plural: Hände.
Plural: Gründe. aus diesem Grund = for this reason.
Familiar; formal: Mutter.
Ruhe! = Quiet! Lass mich in Ruhe! = Leave me alone!
Adjective: tot (dead).
Plural: Stunden.
Ich hoffe es = I hope so.
nach oben = up(wards); da oben = up there.
gestern Abend = last night.
Ich versuche es = I'll try.
eine Art … = a kind of …; auf diese Art = this way.
Schatz is a common way to say darling or honey.
Endlich! = Finally!

words.gloss: about, approximately; (in questions) by any chance
words.notes: In a question it shows surprise: Bist du etwa müde? = You're not tired, are you?
jemandem etwas erzählen = to tell someone something.

words.gloss: to run; to walk; to go (work, be running)
words.notes: du läufst, er läuft; past lief; perfect with sein. Wie läuft's? = How's it going?
Das ist schwer zu sagen = That's hard to say.
Never takes an ending: Er ist anders. jemand anders = someone else.
zum ersten Mal = for the first time.
Plural: Geschichten.
ein wenig = a little. weniger = less.
Ich hole dich ab = I'll pick you up (abholen).
Was bedeutet das? = What does that mean? (meaning of a word or sign)
Das ist nett von dir = That's kind of you.
die Wahrheit sagen = to tell the truth.
Plural: Wochen. nächste Woche = next week.
Verb comes right after it: Deshalb bin ich hier.
Endings like der: welcher Tag, welche Farbe, welches Buch.
Das klappt bestimmt = That will definitely work.
Before a noun it loses the c: ein hoher Berg. Comparative: höher.
Wie alt bist du? = How old are you? Comparative: älter.

words.gloss: to look; to watch (TV, a film)
words.notes: Common in southern Germany and Austria. Schau mal! = Look!
Plural: Länder. auf dem Land = in the country.
Plural also Zimmer.
Plural also Wagen. Often just means car.

words.gloss: to please; (es gefällt mir) I like it
words.notes: The thing liked is the subject: Das Bild gefällt mir = I like the picture.
Viel Spaß! = Have fun! Das macht Spaß = That's fun.
Es ist meine Schuld = It's my fault. Schulden (plural) = debts.
du verlässt, er verlässt; past verließ, perfect verlassen. sich verlassen auf = to rely on.
Zeig mal! = Let me see!
Ist das dein Ernst? = Are you serious? (noun der Ernst)
Plural: Orte.
Plural: Seiten. auf der anderen Seite = on the other side.
Dative for place, accusative for movement.
Er war eben noch hier = He was here just now. Eben! = Exactly!
As a preposition it takes the genitive (spoken often dative).
Plural: Spiele. Das ist kein Spiel = This isn't a game.
Pronounced the French way: SHAHN-se.
meine Freundin often means my girlfriend; eine Freundin = a friend.
Plural: Kriege.
Entschuldigen Sie! = Excuse me! (formal). Entschuldige! = Sorry! (informal)
ins Bett gehen = to go to bed.

words.gloss: bad; (mir ist schlecht) I feel sick
words.notes: Mir ist schlecht = I feel sick.
in die Schule gehen = to go to school.

words.gloss: apology, excuse; (as a word on its own) sorry, excuse me

words.notes: Wörter = separate words; Worte = words spoken (ein paar Worte).
Informal for a man: Wer ist der Typ? = Who's that guy?
du schläfst, er schläft; past schlief.
Plural: Gesichter.
Sends the verb to the end: falls du Zeit hast.

words.gloss: only, just; (in commands) whatever you do; (in questions) on earth
words.notes: Komm bloß nicht zu spät! = Whatever you do, don't be late!
nach unten = down(wards); da unten = down there.
zum Teil = partly.
Comparative: öfter.

words.gloss: to put (upright), place; (eine Frage stellen) to ask
words.notes: Use stellen for things that stand: Stell die Flasche auf den Tisch.
Past trank, getrunken.
einige Tage = a few days; einiges = quite a lot.
Spoken German; in writing use bekommen.
Ehrlich? = Really? Ehrlich gesagt = to be honest.
Plural only: die Eltern.
Er scheint müde zu sein = He seems to be tired. Die Sonne scheint = The sun is shining.
Irregular: das Herz, des Herzens, dem Herzen.
Auf Wiedersehen = Goodbye (polite). Informal: Tschüss.
Ist hier noch frei? = Is this seat free? frei haben = to have time off.
so schnell wie möglich = as fast as possible.
Also a filler: Das ist irgendwie komisch = That's kind of weird.
Das reicht! = That's enough!
Halt dich fest! = Hold on tight!
Plural: Waffen.
Ich kann es kaum glauben = I can hardly believe it.
Das klingt gut = That sounds good.
Plural: Plätze. Nimm Platz = Take a seat.
Familiar; formal: Vater.
Du hast die falsche Nummer = You've got the wrong number.
nicht A, sondern B = not A but B. nicht nur …, sondern auch = not only … but also.
For phone numbers, rooms, sizes. Mathematical number: die Zahl.

words.gloss: earlier; in the past, used to
words.notes: Früher habe ich geraucht = I used to smoke.
For direction: Wohin gehst du? Location: wo.
Takes the dative: alle außer mir. außer Atem = out of breath.
morgen früh = tomorrow morning. Comparative: früher.

words.gloss: to put, set; (sich setzen) to sit down
words.notes: Setz dich! = Sit down! Contrast sitzen = to be sitting.
Zuerst essen wir, dann gehen wir = First we eat, then we go.
ans Telefon gehen = to answer the phone.
Herzlich willkommen! = A warm welcome!
Plural: Pläne.
With movement: Komm hierher! Without movement: hier.
Plural also Fehler. einen Fehler machen = to make a mistake.
nächste Woche = next week. Der Nächste, bitte! = Next, please!
eine Menge = a lot of.
Langsam! = Slow down! Es wird langsam Zeit = It's about time.
A little more formal than schon.
